items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And I had Lucien and McCarthy, Richard. And we played at one of the roughest joints in Dallas.

ctx.x: I know there are a lot of musical families around there.

Well, Oscar Pettiford, that's the band I was supposed to go with when I went to Troy's band. Oh, you were going with the Pettiford? They wanted me. And I had Richard McCarthy from here and Lucian Johnson. And I told them what I was going to do, so I told Richard, I said, Richard, I can get you in this little band if you want to stay. He wanted to come back to New Orleans. So I talked to Pettiford and he only just wanted me in the band. And I told him, no, I had already told Troy that I was going to join him and I…
Did you know the biases? Sure, all of them were there?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: I left there with the banjo, Richard McCarthy, and Lucian Johnson.

ctx.x: He's been following you around, huh?

He was one of the masters. So I said, yeah, I can play something else. So I started out and I tried to improvise one of the three I was playing. He says, that's the same one you've been playing all the time. But in volume it all, huh? He says, that's the same one. Right on the truck then. Yeah, that's right. Well, I left Mardi Gras with three pieces. I left there with the banjo, Richard McCarthy, and Lucian Johnson. And my first stop was Dallas, Texas. And I played at a honky-tonk in Dallas, Texas. It was on the…
Oh, yes. I knew him. Very much in Chicago.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: That was the three that I took out of New Orleans that year going to Dallas.

ctx.x: This is June the 6th, 1961, and I'm Paul Crawford. You were talking about this fellow, one of the first guys you took, you know, when you left New Orleans? No. A banjo player or something?

Yes, I remember that real well. And right here's a picture of him, Paul. Richard McCarthy. I was 16 years old, and Richard I think was 17 or 18. We were in the same bracket there. And then we also had another fellow just a little older, maybe about six or seven months. His name was Johnson. What did he play? He was the alto player. Uh-huh. That was the three that I took out of New Orleans that year going to Dallas.
Did you have a job when you left New Orleans or what were you doing?
